summary: Kazutoshi Soma worked in Buddhist studies, having studied under Meiji Yamada. He held a lecturing post (講師) at Ryukoku University, attested in 1987.
Kazutoshi Ueda (1867–1937) was a scholar of linguistics and Japanology who founded the Linguistic Society of Japan. He studied under Georg von der Gabelentz and Karl Florenz, whom he later succeeded.

Kazuyoshi Hotta specializes in Indology and Buddhist studies. He pursued doctoral studies (博士課程) and served as director (主事) at the University of Tokyo (attested 2007), later holding a fixed-term assistant professorship at Otani University (attested 2015).

Kazuyoshi Kino (1922–2013) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who founded Shinnyokai. He studied at Shudo Junior & Senior High School and the University of Tokyo (1942–1948), later serving as president of Hosen Gakuen College (1989).
Keenan W. Cox is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned an MA at McMaster University under the supervision of James A. Benn (attested 2014).

Kees W. Bolle (1927–2012) worked in religious studies and Indology. He studied at Leiden, Madras, and Chicago under Mircea Eliade. Bolle lectured at Brown (~1960–1964) and became Professor Emeritus of History at UCLA, serving ~1969–1994.

Kehan Ding works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history/archaeology. After a BA at Capital University of Economics and Business, Ding earned a PhD at the University of Edinburgh (2018–2024), where Ding became a Teaching Fellow in 2025.

Kei Kataoka (born 1969) is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and National Sanskrit University. He has taught at Fukuoka University (attested 2006) and serves as Associate Professor at Kyushu University (attested 2008–2026).
Kei Okusa specializes in Buddhist studies. Okusa completed a doctorate in literature (博士(文学)) at Otani University, where Okusa is attested as a faculty member in 2026.

Keiichi Miyamoto (born 1948) is an Indologist and philosopher. He completed his undergraduate, master's, and doctoral studies at the University of Tokyo, studying under Minoru Hara. He taught at Kokugakuin University as lecturer (1986), associate professor (1988), and professor (1995).
Keiji Iwata (1922–2013) was a religious studies scholar who studied at Kyoto University from ~1941 to ~1945. He held academic posts at Tokyo Institute of Technology (~1973–1980) and Otani University.
Keiji Kokubu (1907–1997) was a philosopher who studied at Ryukoku University under Tokuryu Yamauchi. He held academic posts at Ryukoku University, Nanzan University, and Ritsumeikan University.

Keiji Nishitani (1900–1990) was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied at Kyoto University under Nishida and Tanabe, and at Freiburg under Heidegger. He lectured at Otani University (~1928–1935) before serving as professor at Kyoto University (1943–1964).

Keiki Nakayama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Kyoto University (attested 2020). Posts include JSPS research fellow (attested 2020) and visiting scholar at the Göttingen Academy of Sciences and Humanities (attested 2026).

Keiki Yabuki (1879–1939) was a Buddhist studies and religious studies scholar educated at Tohoku Gakuin, Taisho, and the University of Tokyo. He served as professor at Shukyo University (~1919–1926) and Taisho University (~1926–1939).

Keikyo Nakamikado specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Nakamikado held posts as a research collaborator at Bukkyo University (attested 2003) and as a researcher at the Chion'in Research Institute of Jodo Buddhism (attested 2015).

Keinin Hayashi specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. Hayashi served as a lecturer at Waseda University and has held appointments as a full-time researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute (attested 1998, 2026).

Keir Strickland is an archaeologist and Indologist. He studied at Bradford and earned a PhD at Durham under Robin Coningham. Strickland lectured at the University of the Highlands and Islands (2012–2016) before becoming Senior Lecturer at La Trobe University (2016).

Keishin Okamura (1931–2019) was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed undergraduate and doctoral studies at Kyoto University. He was an associate professor at Koyasan University (1959–1973) and served as a professor at Kochi University (~1963–1995).

Keisho Tsukamoto (1929–2010) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his doctorate from Tohoku University. He was a professor at Rissho University (~1964–1980), Tohoku University (~1980–1993), and president of Hosen Gakuen College (~1994–2001).
